title: fix(update): verify paired trusted-proxy gateways with service credentials
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes update and restart verification waiting until its deadline on a healthy trusted-proxy Gateway when the local CLI is already paired but no shared token or password is configured.

## User Impact

Verification can authenticate with the service profile's existing device credentials, including when that profile differs from the invoking shell. Existing shared-token, password, and auth-none probes remain unchanged. No new pairing, credential rotation, configuration option, or schema change is required.

The installed updater runs before candidate activation: unchanged older drivers cannot acquire this caller fix by retrying the same update. For an affected source installation, the canonical owner can drain and stop its existing service, run the existing updater with `--no-restart` against the fixed target, then use the fixed CLI to `gateway restart --preserve-definition`. The stopped-service branch avoids the defective old pre-activation verifier; native update, Doctor, recovery and authentication remain in control. This route has been source-verified against an affected older driver; production execution is still pending the landed fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The verifier forced a null device identity, so the Gateway correctly rejected its handshake. It now reads the existing identity and operator token from the target service environment and carries those prepared credentials through the canonical read-only Gateway client. Server authentication and scope checks remain intact.

The forced-null path was introduced by a5f3623302fd31f917bd83a5abeac56a09a7c737 (#136995). Production delta is +19 lines for explicit service-state ownership; test and documentation changes are separate.

## Evidence

- Actual ephemeral Gateway over real WebSocket transport, using native approval of synthetic CLI credentials during setup: original verifier rejects the handshake; fixed verifier receives real hello version/boot and health.
- Regression separates the client/service profile from ambient Gateway state and verifies unchanged identity/token plus no pending pairing request.
- Fixed call owner and restart siblings: 191 tests passed, including shared token/password/auth-none and trusted-proxy local-password cases.
- Real-Gateway authentication suite: 26 tests passed; the final separate-profile regression also passed.
- Final identity-owner extraction: 164 targeted Gateway, call, and remote-onboarding tests passed. The line-cap guard passes. Local changed checks reached typechecking, which refuses the readonly external dependency donor; exact-head hosted CI supplies the physical-install typecheck.
- Independent P0–P2 review found an initial ambient-state lookup error; the corrected service-environment repair is clean.


CI follow-up: the full non-isolated Linux CLI batch exposed five lifecycle tests that spoof Windows while using unspecified mocked authentication, causing Koffi to select a foreign native addon. Their fixture now explicitly uses auth-none, with unchanged assertions and deadlines. All five failures pass in the full replay (8,585 passed); the untouched `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-artifact.test.ts:246` artifact-cleanup fixture also fails in that Testbox environment and is retained as a separate follow-up. That fixture passed the original hosted CI run. The readonly service-credential production change is unchanged.


## Upgrade verification

The first [published-driver cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35499649622) used released 2026.9.5 against this source-built 2026.9.5 candidate. Core installation and Doctor completed, but plugin convergence correctly refused different bytes for already-pinned same-version Codex, Discord and WhatsApp packages. The harness failed `successful update failed plugin convergence`; this is preserved as a failed cell, and no integrity protection was changed.

The [distinct-version cell](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35501303899) passed: affected published 2026.9.4 updater → exact same candidate artifact, using the real updater with manual restart ownership. Automatic migration, plugin convergence, candidate Gateway startup, health, readiness and status all passed; startup took 62 seconds, health/readiness 1 second each. The separate `update-restart-auth` lane passed on the exact candidate ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35499649622/job/106051779537)). A published-package cell does not establish every source-install plugin provenance transition; an actual source-install cold transition remains an operator acceptance step.

The prior [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35499425346) passed this repair's lanes but exposed a heartbeat fixture lifecycle bug introduced by intervening main #147463. The independent test-only repair landed in #153591; the production worker identity guard stayed unchanged. This branch now incorporates that repaired main at `1874d7b`, preserving identical added/removed repair lines. Fresh actual-Gateway/restart verification passed 119 tests; [fresh integration CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35502995762) passed. Its tested merge `dbaeae3` combines this head with main `24445095`, covering the later cross-install reconciliation changes from #150898.
